name: Oslo
title: Oslo Ship UTM | Thickness Measurement for Fleet Managers
description: UTM and thickness measurement for Oslo shipowners and managers: renewal survey and CAP gauging, pre-purchase condition checks and scrubber piping checks.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement for Oslo Shipowners, Managers and Buyers
intro: Oslo is the commercial heart of Norwegian shipping: shipowners, ship managers, sale-and-purchase brokers, ship financiers and the Norwegian Shipowners' Association all work from the city. Most of the ships controlled from Oslo trade worldwide, while the port itself sees ro-pax ferries, cruise ships, container feeders and product tankers. Atlantis NDT takes gauging scopes from Oslo technical departments and mobilises a team from India to the vessel, wherever it docks.

highlights.p: Oslo brokers and buyers often want structural condition evidence before committing to a second-hand ship. Pre-purchase gauging of holds, ballast tanks and deck, measured against original thicknesses, gives the buyer's technical team firmer ground than records alone.

Technical departments in Oslo and Lysaker run tanker, car-carrier, bulk and gas fleets. We report sister ships to one convention, so condition trends can be compared survey to survey and yard to yard.
Daily ferries to Kiel, Copenhagen and Frederikshavn and summer cruise calls give short windows for piping and deck measurements in the Oslofjord; extensive tank work is left for the docking.

port.h: Oslo: Norway's shipping capital and its working port
p: Oslo's role in ship inspection starts in office buildings rather than on the quay. The city and its neighbouring municipalities host the head offices of Norwegian owners of crude and product tankers, chemical tankers, car carriers, gas carriers and dry-bulk ships, together with ship managers, pool operators, marine insurers and the shipbrokers who arrange sale-and-purchase deals. Ship finance and shipping equities are also traded here, so decisions to buy, sell, refinance or extend the life of a ship are often made in Oslo, and many of them depend on knowing the ship's steel condition.

The port itself is the Oslofjord's main cargo and passenger port. Container feeders call at the Sjursøya terminal, product tankers supply the fuel installations there, and ro-pax ferries run daily to Kiel, Copenhagen and Frederikshavn. Cruise ships berth close to the city centre through the summer season. Ferry turnarounds in Oslo take a matter of hours in the middle of the day, and cruise calls are similar, so neither gives room for extensive tank work, though both allow measurement of machinery-space piping, open decks and selected void spaces when planned with the chief engineer. The Oslofjord approaches are long and sheltered, and ships occasionally wait at anchor inside the fjord for a berth or for orders, which is when short condition checks can be arranged.

For Oslo technical managers the more important question is how to get consistent, reliable gauging on ships that are docking in China, Turkey, Poland or the Middle East. The superintendent wants a TM plan agreed with class before the ship arrives, pre-docking measurements where possible to firm up the steel renewal estimate, and daily reporting during the yard stay. Oslo thickness measurement requests therefore tend to arrive with a full scope, previous reports and a yard name attached, rather than as a request for work in the Oslofjord itself.

facilities.h: Where gauging for Oslo-controlled ships happens
p: Within Oslo, practical gauging locations are the ferry and cruise berths, the Sjursøya container and fuel terminals, and anchorages in the Oslofjord where ships occasionally wait. Ships needing a docking survey in Norway usually go to yards on the west coast, and many Norwegian owners dock in Poland, Lithuania, Turkey or Asia depending on where the ship trades. For the ferries that serve Oslo, the annual docking is the main opportunity for tank and shell measurement, with in-port work limited to what the timetable allows.

For sale-and-purchase work, the location is set by the ship's trading pattern: buyers' inspections often take place at a discharge port or anchorage wherever the ship happens to be, with only a short window agreed with the seller. For fleet programmes, we work wherever the docking is scheduled and report back to Oslo in a single format. Results from each yard are issued in the same layout, with frame and strake references matching the ship's TM plan, so the Oslo technical department can compare them without re-keying. The list below shows the kinds of location involved and the work typically done at each.
list: Oslo ferry berths — piping, car-deck and ramp-area measurements on the Kiel, Copenhagen and Frederikshavn ro-pax ships during midday turnarounds.
Cruise berths near the city centre — machinery-space piping and open-deck plating on cruise ships, planned with the chief engineer.
Sjursøya container and fuel terminals — ballast tank and deck gauging on feeders and product tankers alongside, with cargo tanks kept closed.
Oslofjord anchorages — pre-purchase or on-hire gauging of accessible spaces on ships waiting for berth or orders, with launch access through the agent.
West-coast Norwegian yards — docking-survey and renewal gauging for Oslo-managed ships repaired in Norway.
Overseas docking yards — renewal-survey and CAP gauging for Oslo fleets in Chinese, Turkish, Polish or Middle East yards.

context.h: Norwegian flag, North Sea ECA and the Oslo market
p: Norway is a member of the Paris MoU and, as an EEA state, applies much of the EU's maritime legislation through the EEA Agreement. Many Oslo-controlled ships fly the flag of the Norwegian International Ship Register (NIS); others are registered in the Marshall Islands, Liberia, Malta or Singapore. In every case the gauging scope for a class survey is set by the classification society's rules and the relevant IACS unified requirements. Port state control officers across the Paris MoU region record structural deficiencies that often lead to a request for urgent measurements, and the Oslo technical department then needs a team at the next suitable port.

The Oslofjord lies within the North Sea SOx ECA, so ships trading here burn 0.10% sulphur fuel or run scrubbers. Oslo-controlled tanker and bulk fleets include many scrubber-fitted ships, and the overboard discharge lines and their shell connections are a recurring source of leaks if not measured at each docking. Norwegian owners have also been early movers into LNG, battery and ammonia-ready designs, and retrofits on existing ships bring new penetrations and foundations that need a structural baseline. For older tonnage, the strength of the sale-and-purchase market in Oslo means condition gauging is often the deciding evidence on whether a ship is sold for further trading or for recycling.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs for Oslo owners
jobs.p: Oslo work divides into fleet programmes run by technical departments, transaction-driven gauging for buyers, sellers and financiers, and the occasional short job on a ship in the Oslofjord. The first two account for most of it, and both depend on the team travelling to wherever the ship is. Fleet programmes are usually agreed a season ahead, while transaction work is often confirmed late, once the seller has agreed to access.
list: CAP thickness measurement on a crude tanker controlled from Oslo, carried out at a docking in the Middle East to support charterer vetting for a ship over fifteen years old.
Pre-purchase gauging at an anchorage for an Oslo buyer: holds, topside and hopper tanks and main deck measured on a bulk carrier within a short window agreed with the seller.
Car carrier inspection as part of a fleet gauging programme: car decks, ramps and ballast tanks measured to a common format across sister ships at different yards.
Scrubber piping inspection on an Oslo-managed bulk carrier: wash-water discharge lines and overboard penetrations gauged at docking and compared with the previous survey.
Renewal survey gauging on a chemical tanker at a Polish yard, with daily results sent to the Oslo superintendent for repair decisions.
Bilge, ballast and seawater piping measurements in the engine room of a Kiel ro-pax ferry during an Oslo turnaround, feeding the pipe renewal list for its annual docking.

logistics: Oslo Airport at Gardermoen is the international gateway, with a rail link into the city. Jobs in the port itself need ISPS gate passes for the ferry, cruise and Sjursøya terminals, arranged through the ship's agent; anchorage work in the Oslofjord requires a launch booked by the agent. Most Oslo-commissioned jobs, though, take the team straight to an overseas yard. Norway is a Schengen country, so work there is covered by a Schengen visa; for yards outside Europe, the team applies for the visa of the docking country, which is why we ask for the yard and dates as early as possible.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship for an Oslo buyer before the purchase is concluded?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the seller agrees to access and tank entry. Pre-purchase gauging is usually done in a short window at a discharge port or anchorage. The buyer's technical team chooses the areas, typically cargo holds or tanks, ballast tanks and main deck, and we report readings against the original thicknesses so the condition can be compared with the ship's records and latest class reports.

faqs.q: Do you work in yards outside Norway for Oslo-managed ships?
faqs.a: That is the majority of Oslo-commissioned work. We take the scope and TM plan from the technical department, travel to the yard in China, Turkey, Poland, the Middle East or elsewhere, and report daily during the docking. The visa for the docking country is the main lead-time item, so early notice of the yard and dates makes the difference.

faqs.q: What do Oslo superintendents usually ask for before a renewal survey?
faqs.a: A TM plan agreed with the classification society, previous gauging reports, and pre-docking measurements on the tanks most likely to need steel renewal. Measuring those spaces during a port call before the docking helps firm up the steel estimate in the yard specification and reduces the risk of an unexpected renewal scope once the ship is in dock.

faqs.q: Can gauging be done on a ferry during its Oslo turnaround?
faqs.a: Limited work, yes. The midday turnaround is short and tanks are generally not opened, but machinery-space piping, car-deck plating in accessible areas and open-deck structure can be measured when the chief engineer has planned for it. Ballast and void-space gauging belongs in the annual docking or a planned lay-by.
